subject: Culture
title: Digital Sacred Spaces
description: A quick, practical guide to Digital Sacred Spaces.

hook.text: In 2020 a Japanese temple held funerals over Zoom. The priest chanted. Mourners bowed through laptop screens.

buildup.text: VR churches, online mosques, and digital meditation halls multiplied during the pandemic shutdown.

discovery.text: Second Life had its own churches since 2007. Some hosted weddings, confessions, and weekly services for years.

twist.text: Critics say digital sacred spaces lack embodiment—the physical cues that trigger reverence are missing on screen.

climax.text: Yet online communities form rituals, hierarchies, and pilgrimage-like gatherings that mirror physical religion.

punchline.text: Sacredness may not need walls—just shared attention.

quiz.question: When did Second Life host its first digital churches?
